description:
## Why

Some operators have large PST archives they cannot or do not want to migrate — legal holds, compliance archives, or simply too much data to re-ingest. A read-only PST backend lets stoa serve JMAP Email/get and NNTP ARTICLE requests directly from .pst files in a local directory or a bucket of downloaded PSTs, without any upfront conversion.

This complements the PST import path (stoa-vg6w9): import is for active migration; this backend is for long-term read-only archival access.

## What

Implement PstBlockStore as a read-only IpfsBlockStore (writable = false always).

**Indexing:** On open, enumerate all .pst files in the configured directory, walk every message in each PST, compute CID (SHA-256 of raw message bytes), and record CID → (pst_path, internal_node_id) in a SQLite sidecar index (pst_index.db in the root directory). Index is rebuilt when a PST file's mtime changes or a new PST appears.

**Read path (get_raw):** Look up CID in sidecar, open the PST file, extract message bytes for that node, return them.

**Write path:** Return a clear error — this backend is always read-only. Operators must configure it with writable = false in the composite backend list.

**Bucket of PSTs (S3/GCS/Azure):** Out of scope for initial implementation. Requires downloading PSTs to a local cache directory first; too expensive to access on-the-fly. Document that the PST backend works on local directories only; use the composite backend to pair it with a writable cloud backend.

**Config:**
```toml
[[backend]]
type = "pst"
path = "/archive/pst-files"
writable = false
```

## Implementation

Uses readpst subprocess (same as stoa-vg6w9 Option A) for message extraction, or libpst FFI if that is implemented first. The indexing pass uses readpst to enumerate message IDs and extract bytes; the sidecar maps CIDs to PST-internal node references.

Alternative: run readpst once per PST file to produce a Maildir cache alongside the PST, then serve from the Maildir cache. Simpler (reuses MaildirBlockStore); costs disk space equal to the PST size.

## Acceptance

- PstBlockStore implements IpfsBlockStore with get_raw working and put_raw returning an error
- CID index is built at startup and cached in pst_index.db
- New .pst files dropped into the directory are picked up on next startup (or on a SIGHUP)
- Integration test reads a known message from a sample PST by CID
- writable = false is enforced — put_raw returns IpfsWriteError::WriteFailed with a clear message
notes: The index build time for large PSTs (multi-GB) could be significant. Consider a progress log at startup. The Maildir-cache approach (readpst once → MaildirBlockStore) may be simpler and more robust than maintaining the CID→node sidecar directly.
title: PST read-only block store backend
